stage1.impression: A clear cylinder with a blue core and bubble voids sits on a pale disc on a grey satin platter against a flat mid-grey ground. The glass edges are crisp but the whole set is one light-grey value, so nothing reads as precious or as a record. The lower third of the object goes to near-black navy, where the voids disappear.

blocking_9: The LP reads as black vinyl with concentric groove sheen (lum_median below about 90 off the highlight), not as grey brushed metal (now 95 to 199).

The cove reads as a dark neutral (lum_median about 35 to 75), not mid grey (now 120 to 147), so the acrylic's silhouette and rims separate from the ground by at least 40 levels (the right edge step is now -10.5).
The voids in the lower stratum are visible as silver-rimmed lenses: region 1000-1140 x 660-800 now has median 9.4 and 1.35% crushed.
No hard reflected line crosses the LP behind the base (now a 4 px line, step 13, at y about 660 on the left and 715 on the right).
The LP's far edge no longer runs tangent to the object's top rim at y about 380-400. This needs a camera elevation change, judged after the set is darkened.
The right flank of the acrylic is not a flat white slab (1080-1230 x 480-600 now median 216, 1.26% clipped).

changes.problem: The seamless cove is specified near-black but renders mid grey, so the clear acrylic has nothing dark to read its edges and voids against, and the black LP reflects it as grey.

evidence.measured: Background lum_median 137.6 (p5 118, p95 173). The vertical profile at x 800-1000 rises from 120 to 147 toward the horizon. The right silhouette edge step is only -10.5 levels.

changes.expected: The cove reads as a deep neutral, lum_median 40-70, keeping a gentle lift toward the horizon. The acrylic rims and the void rims stand out as bright lines against it.

changes.problem: The overhead floods the set, and at this grazing angle the LP mirrors it and the cove, so the black record reads as grey metal.

evidence.measured: LP back-left lum_median 179.8. LP back-right (1450-1700 x 450-600) is 95.4. LP front-left (100-400 x 950-1150) is 198.8. A black vinyl surface should sit well below 100 off its highlight.

changes.expected: The LP back-left drops to about 60-100 and keeps a soft sheen gradient instead of a uniform grey. The object's top face stays lit but not flooded.

changes.problem: The lower stratum of the object is crushed to black-navy, so the voids sealed at the lower bond line, the frame's subject, are invisible there.

evidence.measured: lum_median 9.4, p5 3.8, crush_pct 1.35, r_median 0. The left part (600-840 x 660-800) is median 35.5.

change.from: white card 600 x 160 at y = -520, unpowered
change.to: make the card an emitter: an area light 600 x 160 mm at (0, -520, 40), behind the camera and below the lens axis, aimed at the target (0, 0, 14), 4 W, #FFFFFF

changes.expected: A low frontal fill enters the side wall under the critical angle, so the lower voids show silver TIR rims against the blue. The region lifts to a median of about 30-60 without flattening the blue to grey.

changes.problem: The LP has no grooves, so it reads as a satin steel platter and the object as sitting on a machine part rather than on a record.

evidence.measured: LP front-right lum_median 139.8, lum_range 28.8: one smooth value with no groove structure. The front-left is 198.8, a broad metallic sheen.

change.to: black vinyl: base colour #0B0B0C, roughness 0.3, with a concentric groove bump (pitch about 0.1 mm, gentle strength) or anisotropic tangential roughness, so highlights form radial arcs through the sheen

changes.expected: The LP reads as black with thin bright arcs where the overhead and key catch the grooves. Off-highlight areas fall to a median of about 25-70.

changes.problem: The right rim light makes the acrylic's right flank a flat white slab that clips, instead of a graded edge highlight.
changes.expected: The right flank becomes a narrower bright edge with the interior visible behind it. The median drops to about 150-195 and nothing clips beyond a thin line.

changes.problem: The key spills a broad sheen over the LP's front-left, unbalancing the frame left-to-right by about 70 levels on the record.

evidence.measured: LP front-left lum_median 198.8 against 139.8 at the front-right. The horizontal profile across y 1000-1150 runs 207, 187, 173, 136, 134, 168, 139, 150.

changes.expected: The front-left LP sheen comes down to sit within about 30 levels of the right side. The object's left face keeps its void rims lit.

changes.problem: A hard reflected horizon line crosses the LP right at the object's base, cutting the label disc visually in two.

evidence.measured: Edge step 13.0 levels over a 4 px width at y about 668. On the right (1400-1460 x 690-750) the step is 11.1 over 10 px.

changes.expected: The reflected cove horizon blurs into a soft gradient. With c1's darker cove it falls below about 6 levels of step.

out_of_scope.request: Make the lower stratum's tint thinner and paler, closer to a 3 mm pale-blue lamina.
out_of_scope.why: The lower 150 px of the object (y 640-810) renders as a deep navy band (r_median 0-29), not a thin pale-blue stratum. That may be a tint-absorption or geometry error, but the acrylic's absorption and the strata are fixed. Verify them against the maker's transmission chart and the model.

out_of_scope.request: Raise the camera (z 170 to about 220) so the LP's far edge sits clear above the object's top rim.
out_of_scope.why: The far edge at y about 380-400 runs tangent to the back of the top rim, which flattens the depth. Judge it after c1/c2 darken the set, because a camera move invalidates every region test above. It is held back for that reason, not because it is fixed.
